canal_p21_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_001.text: The fiftieth morning smelled of wet ash from the grain-house stove. The older route book showed a public return reach beyond its rear sheds, drawn as a thin line between storage yards and water. The current map stopped at the sheds. Yue joined the path officer during her accepted inspection interval, with Luo carrying the old keeper's recollections rather than a second authority to settle title. Han sent his foreman to identify private platforms. The foreman brought a measuring cord and said he had hoped the town would finally run out of old paper.

canal_p21_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_002.text: Behind the first shed the path became a corridor between two piles of empty crates. Its outer edge had fallen toward the water, and somebody had tied a mooring rope across the remaining passage. Yue stopped before the rope. The officer inspected the sound approach from above and marked the narrow limit. Luo recognized the place where she had eaten quiet suppers years ago. "It was wider in my memory." The foreman looked at the water. "Everything is wider before you have to move goods through it." Neither offered to test the edge with a body.

canal_p21_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_003.text: The mooring rope belonged to a small covered workboat lodged against an old timber fender. Its owner had moved upstream after the storm and left a note at the wrong landing. The officer's ordinary receiver located the current contact before anyone cut the line. The boat did not become public scrap because it obstructed a common route. Yue could see a sound corner of the old tow return beyond it, unreachable from the wet edge they stood on. The rope blocked the way like a sentence whose missing subject everybody had been trying to invent.

canal_p21_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_004.text: A cabinet maker occupied the second shed under a private rent agreement. He had stacked boards where the newer map appeared to end, believing the dry strip belonged to his landlord. His apprentice was rubbing a table leg with wax and looked relieved that the argument did not concern the finish. The cabinet maker produced his lease. It described the shed floor and private yard boundary, not the common return shown in the older route book. He asked why no official had mentioned that when he moved in. The officer said the question deserved an answer, not his immediate guilt.

canal_p21_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_005.text: The landlord arrived with a key and a hat. He remembered a keeper allowing crates there during one hard winter. Luo knew the keeper's name and said he had died before she took the post. Temporary storage permission might explain the practice without transferring title. The landlord disliked the distinction until the cabinet maker pointed to the rent he had paid for what he thought he could use. Their private dispute would need the actual agreement and account. Yue measured no compensation she had authority to award. The public route question could be examined without deciding the tenants' entire past.

canal_p21_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_006.text: The path officer found a boundary marker behind the second pile, still standing but covered in green moss. He brushed only the face needed to read its old route number and compared it with the book. Yue copied the number while the foreman held the cord clear of water. The marker placed the return on the common strip. It did not make every raised patch beside it public or turn the cabinet maker's boards into canal stock. Luo crouched to inspect it and rose more carefully than usual. Age was beginning to have practical opinions about forgotten monuments.

canal_p21_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_007.text: A former boatwoman watched from the sound yard while they worked. She said the return had been used by workers walking upstream after releasing tow lines, when cargo boats themselves stayed below. It was not an alternate channel for barges. The narrow old drawing had invited a grander story in the market. Yue asked where the woman had actually walked and when. She gave dates tied to her daughter's marriage and one memorable broken shoe. The officer kept the recollection beside the marker and current measurements. Her shoe could locate a memory, but it could not certify today's footing.

canal_p21_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_008.text: The cabinet maker offered a narrow passage through his shed so the party could inspect beyond the unsafe outer strip. The officer described exactly who would enter, for what interval, and what they would carry. The tenant agreed; his apprentice moved the wax pot away before their boots reached it. Yue carried her rule under one arm rather than dragging it across the unfinished furniture. Inside, warm wood smelled unlike the public mud. The cabinet maker watched them pass with the strained courtesy of a person who had invited a necessary nuisance into his day's paid work.

canal_p21_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_009.text: From the sound rear threshold they could see the far return reach without stepping onto it. A broken fender had twisted into the old walking line; beyond that, packed gravel still held above ordinary water. The inspection identified separate problems: private obstruction, current damaged edge, and a public route lost from the working copy. Clearing one would not solve the others. Luo stared toward the quiet bend. "I suppose I should feel vindicated." The cabinet maker answered from inside, "I would settle for knowing where to put the table legs." Yue preferred his more manageable wish.

canal_p21_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_010.text: The path officer closed the unsafe outer portion and marked the sound approach used for the inspection. A later repair would require an estimate and actual authorization outside the exhausted small path task. There was no emergency justification for Yue to haul crates, move a private boat, or command the frame into a forgotten reach. The present task could make the route visible and prevent a dangerous shortcut. The tenant accepted the temporary marks after seeing their extent. He asked for a current copy, not another assurance that somebody somewhere had a book.

canal_p21_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_011.text: On returning through the shed Yue snagged her coat on a splintered rack. She stopped before pulling against it and let the apprentice free the cloth with a small wooden wedge. The coat acquired a tiny tear anyway. He apologized, then said the rack was scheduled to be planed after the paid table order. Yue paid nothing for his immediate voluntary help, but thanked him and asked where she could mend the tear without using his working bench. He pointed to an empty stool. Luo waited while Yue made a rough repair whose crookedness delighted the foreman.

canal_p21_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_012.text: The cabinet maker's landlord wanted the inspection record to say the tenant had created the obstruction. Some boards were his; the crates had belonged to an earlier renter, and the moored boat to neither. The officer recorded the actual ownership information and unanswered contacts. Yue saw the cabinet maker stop clenching his jaw when the names stayed distinct. His landlord's clean hat began dripping where mist had gathered on its brim. An argument about a missing map could not be shortened by finding the nearest renter willing to be blamed for everything on the ground.

canal_p21_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_013.text: The foreman identified two private loading platforms stored there by Han's father. Their present owner was Han, whose gear inventory did not confuse them with public bank work. One was sound enough to move under the merchant's own handling arrangement; the other needed private inspection before use. Han could arrange their removal from the common return after receiving the current measurements. The platforms' private title did not authorize their indefinite placement on the route. Luo nodded toward the clean hat. The landlord pretended to be examining the boundary marker instead.

canal_p21_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_014.text: The boat owner answered before evening. He would return on the fifty-first morning with his own crew, at the ordinary water level the officer had described. They would move the workboat using its checked mooring gear and accepted safe shore positions. If the bank or level proved unsuitable, he would wait and arrange another method. Yue read the reply rather than treating the date as a completed removal. The crew's cost remained the owner's private expense. The common route would gain space only when the boat and rope actually moved, not when a letter promised they would.

canal_p21_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_015.text: At the office Pei found a newer map annotation copied from a storage permission without its end date. It explained how the working return line had disappeared. The original route reference and current marker still supported common access; the annotation did not grant a perpetual private yard. She preserved both copies. Yue expected the clerk to condemn the unnamed copyist. Instead Pei looked tired. "Someone wrote the convenient half," she said. "Someone else needed it to be convenient." The correction would need to reach the people using the place, not merely replace a page on her shelf.

canal_p21_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_016.text: The cabinet maker requested a temporary arrangement for his boards while the landlord checked the private lease boundary. Han offered space for one short stack in his own yard at a quoted modest storage price. The tenant preferred to shorten his pile inside the shed, even though it would slow the table order. He did not want another private bill. Yue noted his choice for the public obstruction plan with his agreement. Clear access had real costs to people whose private work was useful and lawful. Correcting the map could not make those costs vanish into gratitude.

canal_p21_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_017.text: The ordinary winter schedule did not need the entire old return reopened immediately. Its safe alternative route was longer but already known. The officer proposed keeping the damaged portion closed while clearing private goods from the sound common strip and restoring the route to the current working copy. A separate estimate would address the edge and broken fender. Luo disliked how little water this plan appeared to move. Yue reminded her that a walking return was not a flood diversion. The keeper threw a crust to a passing duck and said even the duck probably knew that now.

canal_p21_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_018.text: Han arrived at the office after inspecting the foreman's drawing. He agreed to remove the listed private platforms under his own crew's appointment, without charging the public lease before it began. His wife checked the handling price and signed their private work sheet. The broken fender was not his platform. The officer would identify its actual route authority before repair or disposal. Han seemed relieved not to possess every piece of old wood near the canal. Tian said this was a modest improvement over wishing to own every household too. The merchant sighed and accepted the deserved blow.

canal_p21_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_019.text: The winter assistant copied the route correction as a current closing-week task under the administrative allowance. Her separately funded winter post would begin after closure and last only its accepted two months. She used a broad line to distinguish the common return from the private shed threshold. Pei watched the pen move without correcting its size. Yue noticed the older clerk could read the resulting number from across the table. The assistant did not ask whether this proved her useful forever. She asked whether the route notice needed two copies for the two approaches, a question with an answer.

canal_p21_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_020.text: Tian came to mend Yue's rough coat repair after seeing it. She wanted to undo the crooked stitches; Yue refused to have a private customer order delayed for her sleeve. They agreed Tian would show her the better fold during a personal interval, then let her sew it herself. The lesson took place beside the keeper's stove. Tian removed one stitch, explained the folded edge, and returned the needle. Yue needed three tries. Luo admired the result loudly enough to make clear she had enjoyed the failures even more. Yue wore the coat anyway.

canal_p21_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_021.text: The cabinet maker's apprentice brought the current route notice back with a penciled question. The marked sound strip seemed to cross a stack he had already moved. The assistant checked the drawing against the officer's measurement and corrected a misplaced line before the notice went up. The apprentice had prevented a false instruction simply by reading the thing he was expected to obey. Pei thanked him without offering him an unpriced new duty. He asked whether he could return to the table leg. Yue said he could, since unlike their paperwork it already had an owner waiting for it.

canal_p21_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_022.text: The three useful next intervals lay on the fifty-first morning. One would witness the private workboat's actual move from sound positions. Another would compare the public map and the tenant's practical receiving copy at the shed. The third would help inspect the current winter walking alternative with Luo while the damaged return remained closed. All stayed within ordinary tasks and existing appointments. No branch would award ownership of the forgotten reach. Yue could choose where to see the correction meet actual people, leaving the other named workers to complete and report their own bounded work.

canal_p21_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_023.text: The former boatwoman offered to attend the map comparison as a voluntary witness to the route she remembered. She would not be asked to walk the damaged edge or prove her memory by balancing above water. She laughed at Yue's careful invitation. "I was agile once. It was never a legal qualification." The officer agreed to hear her from the sound shed threshold. Her daughter would bring her ordinary stool. Yue had begun to value stools more than she expected; they allowed people to remain in a conversation without pretending every contributor had the same legs.

canal_p21_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_024.text: At the landing the workboat owner's crew checked their private lines before tomorrow's move. Yue saw the old rope they had left blocking the return and the sound replacement coiled beside it. They would carry no loaded cargo during the maneuver. The owner asked where he could tie afterward; the public landing receiver gave the actual permitted berth and interval. There was room, but not an indefinite free place. He wrote the end date on his own sheet. His delayed return had already cost him one private job, which made him impatient without making the narrow bank stronger.

canal_p21_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_025.text: Luo walked the longer winter alternative once before supper and found a loose shutter swinging across its narrowest section. It belonged to a laundry shed, whose owner repaired the hinge with her own worker. The keeper returned after the repair and checked the clear width. Yue heard the report and marked the actual time. It was an ordinary private repair supporting a public walk, not another draw from the exhausted emergency materials purse. The washerwoman said Luo could thank her by not throwing duck crusts onto the washing steps. The keeper denied everything except the duck.

canal_p21_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_026.text: The night was cold enough that the boats creaked against their lines. Yue read Ren's acceptance and then stopped herself from planning an excuse in case the orchard review was difficult. The ordinary departure remained booked. Her final canal work now had actual end points: the route correction, the cause hearing, the receiving report, and closure. The forgotten reach could be made safer without becoming her next permanent occupation. She folded the map beside the commission folder rather than inside her pack. In the morning it would go to people who would still be here after she left.

canal_p21_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_027.text: At dawn the fifty-first day looked deceptively gentle. Mist rested on the canal without moving the current marks. Han's crew arrived for its private platform handling; the boat crew stood at the sound permitted berth; the office assistant carried two current route notices. Luo had eaten breakfast and was therefore almost agreeable. Yue put on her newly mended coat. The small fold held when she raised her arm. Tian saw it from her window and lifted one thumb, a quieter approval than the keeper's applause and more valuable because it came from somebody who knew the stitches.

canal_p21_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_028.text: The officer repeated the actual ground limit before work began. Nobody would step onto the undermined edge to make a rope angle more convenient. The workboat would move only while its inspected gear and ordinary level met the plan. The map comparison would take place on sound private ground under the tenant's current permission. Luo's winter walk used the known alternative and its repaired shutter clearance. Yue checked the accepted interval she could spend. These boundaries did not diminish the three tasks; they allowed each to finish without requiring another night's emergency.

canal_p21_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_029.text: The canal divided the morning's noises: a private boat line sliding through a checked ring, the cabinet maker's plane biting into an unfinished leg, and Luo calling from the longer foot route. Yue stood beside the officer with the older book open to the restored return. The faded line had finally become a place people could discuss without claiming the whole world around it. She chose which current task to witness first. The others remained in their actual appointments, with reports due before the day's corrections reached the public board.

choices.text: Witness the private workboat's safe removal.
Compare the route and the tenant's receiving map.
Walk the usable winter alternative with Luo Zhen.

canal_p21_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_030.text: The private workboat owner walked the sound shore positions with the officer before casting off. Yue stayed behind the marked edge, watching the old blocking rope rather than imagining she could catch a boat if the maneuver failed. Two crew members checked the replacement line and the permitted berth downstream. The boat carried only its ordinary gear. The owner had wanted to bring stored boards along to save another trip; the officer held him to the current unloaded plan. He grumbled, removed the boards himself, and put them on his own sound yard.

canal_p21_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_031.text: When the old rope came slack, one crew member began to unfasten it from the weathered ring. The ring shifted in its bed. He stopped and called the owner rather than finishing the easy pull. The inspection had found sound gear but not guaranteed every fixing hidden behind it. They secured the boat from the already checked alternate position, keeping the doubtful ring unloaded. Yue marked the observation for the route authority. The owner looked at the ring as though it had personally wasted his morning. His crew looked grateful not to be made to argue with him about it.

canal_p21_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_032.text: The crew controlled the boat with its checked private lines and ordinary current. It moved a short distance from the fender, exposing a smear of trapped reeds against the hull. Nothing spectacular happened. Yue watched the clearance until the bow reached the safe angle named in the plan. The owner repeated the next instruction without changing it to gain speed. From the shed the cabinet maker's apprentice leaned out and cheered too soon. The officer sent him back from the doorway edge. The boat still had to reach its actual permitted berth before anybody claimed success.

canal_p21_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_033.text: A small loose board floated out from beneath the hull. The crew let it drift rather than reaching beyond their footing to catch it. It held no name or fitting that identified private ownership. The landing receiver could recover it later with the ordinary safe bank tool if conditions allowed. Yue felt the old impulse to use a clever command for such a trivial object and disliked recognizing it. The useful act was leaving it alone. She kept watching the loaded line and let the floating board pass through the sunlight toward a place where hands might safely reach it.

canal_p21_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_034.text: At the permitted berth the crew made the checked mooring arrangement and confirmed the boat settled clear of the public walking approach. The receiver recorded the start and end of the stay. The owner had paid for the private move through his own crew's appointment. He asked whether the public route could now open, pointing at the rope he had removed. The officer showed the separate damaged edge and broken fender. Removing one obstruction had solved one problem. The owner stared briefly, then nodded. Yue appreciated the nod more than an apology for the original note at the wrong landing.

canal_p21_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_035.text: They coiled the old blocking rope and handed it to the actual boat owner, who chose to retire it from loads after inspecting the wear. It did not become commission supply because Yue had witnessed its removal. He kept its sound short length for private tying jobs and marked that limited use. The doubtful shore ring remained unloaded and visibly noted for the route authority. Luo arrived with the restored map copy and said she had eaten beside that ring for years. The owner said he hoped her supper had been lighter than his boat. She chose not to answer.

canal_p21_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_036.text: The route's sound inner strip was now visible beyond the rope's former line. Yue compared its present width with the current sketch from the shed threshold. The officer allowed no walk onto the closed outer portion merely because the view looked improved. The cabinet maker moved his remaining boards inside as agreed, finishing the obstruction part within his own private time. He complained about losing elbow room at the bench. The apprentice said the table legs could not complain and were therefore preferable colleagues. The cabinet maker ordered him to wax them before he became too articulate.

canal_p21_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_037.text: Han's crew removed the sound private platform under its accepted handling arrangement, using its checked private gear from the inspected yard positions. The doubtful platform remained set aside for private condition assessment and would not be used for public loading. It could be moved safely as an unloaded object under the separately inspected plan, but today's crew did not improvise that plan at the water edge. Han booked the required private inspection. The current record distinguished removal done from removal pending. Yue had learned to distrust tidy lists whose last column could contain both without anybody noticing.

canal_p21_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_038.text: The boat owner visited the office to correct the landing where future notes would be delivered. His earlier message had gone to a clerk who no longer handled this reach. The winter assistant changed the contact and retained the date of correction. Nobody charged the public budget for his private crew's lost work or the boat move. He accepted that, although he asked where a general complaint belonged. Pei gave him a real address. A place to complain was preferable to pretending a correctly paid task meant a person no longer felt wronged by the day.

canal_p21_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_039.text: Yue signed the current receiving note with the moved boat, clear old rope line, doubtful shore ring, and still-closed edge kept distinct. The officer would send the actual condition report to the ordinary route authority. The boat crew returned to its private work. At the landing the loose board had reached the sound bank and was recovered by the receiver's ordinary long hook without anyone entering the water. Yue watched him set it in the unidentified salvage place. It was not a prize. The morning had made a small reach less obstructed and left the next decision honestly visible.

canal_p21_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_040.text: The cabinet maker set three stools inside the sound shed threshold. The former boatwoman took the best-lit one and placed her hands on her knees. Yue sat beside the current map, while the officer opened the original route book. The landlord remained standing, perhaps hoping this would make him appear less involved. The apprentice carried a table leg through the gathering and said he would continue his paid work quietly. The boatwoman told him quiet work was the most suspicious kind. His plane began making enough noise to satisfy her.

canal_p21_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_041.text: They compared the marker number, the old common return line, and the tenant's lease boundary without treating one drawing as the whole truth of the place. The older book gave the route reference; the current measurements showed which footing had failed. The private agreement defined the shed and yard actually rented. The landlord wanted the map correction to leave rent untouched until his lawyer looked at it. The tenant wanted the space he believed he had paid for. Yue wrote the two requests on separate leaves. Their private dispute could not be settled by erasing the public route again.

canal_p21_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_042.text: The former boatwoman described returning upstream after a tow job, carrying only her line and lunch wrapper. She pointed from the stool to the gravel patch she remembered, then stopped where memory no longer matched the present edge. The officer noted the limit. The landlord asked whether boats had ever loaded there. "A basket or two, when someone was lazy," she replied. "That is not the route's purpose." Yue appreciated her refusing to make every remembered convenience a right. Her daughter brought warm water, and the witness interrupted a question until she had drunk it.

canal_p21_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_043.text: The tenant showed where his boards could fit inside without touching the unfinished furniture. His apprentice suggested a raised rack fixed to the shed's own sound posts. That would cost materials and labor, neither already paid by the public commission. The cabinet maker priced it from his private stock and current paid work schedule. He could complete it after the table delivery. Until then the shorter temporary pile remained safe and clear of the common strip. Yue recorded no new public purchase. A lawful route correction had left him with an inconvenient but possible workshop rather than a vanishing livelihood.

canal_p21_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_044.text: The landlord inspected the lease wording privately with his tenant while Yue and the officer waited outside on sound ground. Their voices rose, fell, and rose again. When they returned, the landlord offered a written reduction of one copper on the next month's rent because the usable private storage area was less than the tenant had reasonably understood. They left older disputed months for their actual private review, not a rushed public verdict. The tenant accepted the limited amendment after reading it. Yue witnessed its date with permission but did not copy their entire account into the canal book.

canal_p21_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_045.text: Pei's assistant brought the corrected practical notice, showing the private threshold, sound common strip, and closed damaged edge in broad separate marks. The tenant read it from where his apprentices would approach. He found the wording clear enough to use. The landlord asked why his name appeared only beside private contact information rather than in the public route title. The officer answered from the surviving route reference. There was no insult in the missing honor, only a boundary. The boatwoman laughed and said she too had lived beside the water without obtaining a deed to its next bend.

canal_p21_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_046.text: A customer arrived to collect the unfinished table and was irritated by the gathering. The cabinet maker explained the short delay and gave the revised actual delivery interval. He did not blame Yue for every late shaving of wood. The customer inspected the legs, accepted the new time, and left a deposit under their private order. The apprentice returned to planing with renewed speed. Yue moved the map away from his flying shavings. She was glad the public meeting could end before it consumed another private transaction simply by considering itself more important than the furniture.

canal_p21_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_047.text: The former boatwoman approved the quoted account of her own past walking use and declined to have her age printed beside it. Her daughter said the whole town knew. "Then the paper can afford to be discreet," she replied. Pei's assistant removed the unnecessary figure. Yue kept the remembered use separate from the officer's present condition finding. The witness had contributed a real voice without becoming a guarantee that anyone could still walk where she once had. She rose with her daughter's ordinary help and left the best-lit stool for someone who would need it next.

canal_p21_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_048.text: The corrected map copy went to both approaches and the current route office. The lost return was again a common walking reference, with its damaged portion closed and a separate assessment pending. The shed remained rented private space under the tenant's actual amendment. Its boards remained his, and the landlord's clean hat remained only a hat. Yue found herself smiling at that last unrecorded fact. The cabinet maker thanked the officer for explaining where the table legs could stand. He thanked Yue for not using his workbench as an altar for all the town's old grievances.

canal_p21_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_049.text: When the meeting ended, Yue helped the apprentice sweep the shavings only after he accepted the voluntary offer. She had completed her appointed comparison and was free to leave. He asked whether she was a surveyor or a cultivator. She said she was learning to be useful at a few things and making frequent errors in all of them. He considered this, then showed her the wrong cut hidden on the table leg's inner side. His employer had approved a sound correction. Yue looked at her mended coat and decided not to offer a competitive account of her own stitches.

canal_p21_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_050.text: Luo set out along the winter alternative in her ordinary coat, not the soaked emergency one. The longer route passed the laundry shed, turned behind the grain store, and reached the known safe landing. Yue joined during her accepted walk interval. The keeper carried no special power source, only the warning list and a little food. "I am testing the condition under which I actually become pleasant," she said, opening the food parcel. Yue suggested that the condition might be impossible to rate. Luo handed her a small turnip slice as if this were an appropriate penalty for insolence.

canal_p21_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_051.text: The repaired shutter hinge no longer swung into the narrow walk. The washerwoman showed them the actual fastening and asked Luo to stop checking it every time she passed. Its condition belonged in the route observation, but not every ordinary round needed to become a private inspection. Luo apologized and looked uncomfortable enough that Yue did not add a comment. The woman offered them the dry space to compare the warning call. The words carried clearly past the closed shutter under the present quiet conditions. They recorded those conditions without claiming that rain or cart noise had been tested there.

canal_p21_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_052.text: At the grain-store turn a new stack of sacks narrowed the path. The store clerk had put them there for one morning, expecting to shift them after the boat arrived. Luo asked for the public line to remain clear now. He complained that the cargo had nowhere convenient to wait. Yue showed him the sound private loading space his own receiver had kept empty. Moving the sacks used the store's current appointed workers, not an offer to borrow nearby households. They cleared the passage while the clerk muttered about the unreasonable width of human shoulders.

canal_p21_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_053.text: The alternative reached a little covered stair whose roof leaked near one corner. It was not a new boarding point for heavy cargo; walkers could stand on the sound dry part and use the safe steps. The keeper reported the roof condition through ordinary maintenance rather than promising Yue would fix it with magic. A traveler waited there with a basket of eggs and asked whether the old return had opened. Luo gave the actual partial closure and the longer route. The traveler sighed, then checked her basket lid before setting out. The eggs mattered more than the map's elegance.

canal_p21_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_054.text: Beyond the stair they met the former check worker carrying his completed private inventory pay home. He used the longer route and asked whether it would stay clear in snow. Luo explained the appointed keeper checks and the public notice, with fresh work requiring actual authority if weather exceeded ordinary service. He wanted to help when called at a real price. Yue added his chosen winter contact to the current notice list. He told them his sister had already claimed half the coat he wore. Luo said this seemed a more reliable labor arrangement than any guild she had known.

canal_p21_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_055.text: The far receiver practiced the full spoken return from the safe covered place. A passing flock of geese briefly made conversation impossible. Luo waited, glaring at them as if they had failed a scheduled appointment. Yue asked the receiver to repeat the instruction after the birds moved past. The answer came correctly. The test accepted present audibility with an obvious interruption, not a magical phrase that cut through all sound. The receiver laughed and said the geese ought to be on the list of unavailable staff. Luo wrote no such entry, although Yue saw her consider it.

canal_p21_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_056.text: On the way back they found a child dragging a plank toward the closed old reach. He wanted to make his own bridge to the fishing place. Yue stopped him on sound ground and asked who knew where he had gone. His aunt came from the laundry shed when Luo called. They returned the plank to its actual owner and explained the hollow edge. The boy protested that adults had used that route for years. Luo showed him the present damage from the safe point. He accepted the difference grudgingly, which was still better than being carried home from water.

canal_p21_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_057.text: The aunt requested a lower marker because children could slip beneath the ribbon without noticing its words. The officer accepted the proposed additional mark and fitted it within the ordinary closure arrangement. Yue witnessed its placement from the sound approach; no new household guarding duty came with the request. The boy helped choose where it would catch his eye and wanted his name painted on it. His aunt declined that honor. Luo offered him the meaningless wet rope tuft recovered earlier only if its current owner agreed. Yue reminded her that the fisherman already considered himself rich in such treasure.

canal_p21_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_058.text: The winter walk ended with the clear shutter, shifted sacks, practiced receiver, and lower closure marker recorded. It had used the known sound alternative rather than proving the damaged old route unnecessary forever. Its longer distance would inconvenience real workers, and the separate assessment could still justify a later repair. Luo could now explain where to walk while that happened. Yue checked the actual accepted interval and closed her notes. The keeper sat on a public bench and finished the turnip parcel, watching a cargo crew use the path without squeezing sideways past the grain sacks.

canal_p21_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_059.text: Luo asked whether Yue would remember this place after the forest road grew difficult. Yue said she would probably remember the geese before the map. The keeper looked satisfied. "That is accurate authorship." They watched the afternoon light gather on the ordinary canal level. The storm had left damage, the correction had left inconveniences, and the walk had left nobody hungry enough to argue further. Yue took the empty food wrapper to the proper bin and returned to the office with the actual route report. Behind her, Luo began the shorter round she was genuinely paid to make.

canal_p21_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_060.text: The fiftieth and fifty-first days left the old return visible in the working map again. Its common walking reference was supported by the route book, the surviving marker, and the present comparison. Its damaged outer portion stayed closed. The cabinet maker's shed and private yard remained distinct from it. Pei read the receiving reports aloud while the new assistant sorted the copies. The former boatwoman's remembered use added a human account without certifying today's ground. Yue watched the officer sign the current condition. The signature did not need to pretend the place had become whole.

canal_p21_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_061.text: The private workboat and blocking rope had moved to the permitted berth under the owner's actual crew appointment. The doubtful old shore ring remained unloaded for assessment. Han's sound platform had been removed, and his doubtful one had a separate private handling inspection booked. The public return therefore held fewer obstructions, but still needed its damaged edge and fender addressed under a future funded road task. The path officer entered the separate estimate request before leaving. Luo asked whether its receipt had an actual number. He showed it to her without taking offense.

canal_p21_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_062.text: The tenant moved the last short stack clear of the common line and carried his paid table order to the agreed delivery. His private rent amendment reduced the next month by one copper; older questions remained with the actual parties. The apprentice brought Pei the acknowledged practical notice and then hurried back to his plane. Yue watched him go with shavings caught in his hair. He had contributed a useful correction and still had his own craft to finish. The public book could remember that without making the canal the center of his life.

canal_p21_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_063.text: Luo and the young keeper accepted the longer winter walk as the current usable route. The repaired shutter, clear grain turn, and additional low closure mark were checked under their actual conditions. A smaller marker could catch a child's eye without becoming a fence capable of holding a grown load. The warning receivers remained named people with real replies. Pei struck out a sentence that called the route foolproof. Luo said she had met too many fools to sign such a claim. The assistant changed it to the accepted condition and handed the keeper the broad copy.

canal_p21_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_064.text: The former boatwoman returned her borrowed stool and lingered to look at the corrected map. Her daughter wanted to know whether reopening the whole return might happen before winter. The officer's estimate was not yet approved, and nobody promised a date simply because both women hoped for one. The older woman nodded. "I came to tell you where I walked, not make your wages endless." Yue thanked her again. At the door she asked the clerk to put her name beside her actual chosen words. She liked the new broad lettering and said so without apologizing for her eyesight.

canal_p21_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_065.text: Han's private crew inspected the doubtful platform from the sound yard. They found one rotten joint and chose a rated dry handling method that kept the piece unloaded and away from the unstable bank. The merchant authorized the quoted private cost. By evening the platform had been moved out of the common strip and marked against use until repaired. His foreman brought the actual completion note to the route office. The public lease had still not begun. Clearing his own stored gear did not create another invoice against the future four-copper monthly gear fee.

canal_p21_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_066.text: Tian met the cabinet maker's apprentice at the grain stall and admired the finished table leg. He admired her sail sample in return, asking why the corner seam doubled. They discussed tension and grain as if the canal dispute had never required them to speak. Yue listened over her bowl of rice, enjoying a conversation in which she knew too little to dominate. Tian explained one fold and then stopped explaining to eat. The apprentice admitted his first leg had been cut short. Neither treated the admission as a request for the other to judge an entire future career.

canal_p21_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_067.text: Bao heard about the rotten platform and offered one brief private drawing observation within his continuing light-work limit. Han declined to rush its repair before winter because the smaller loading operation could manage without it. Bao looked disappointed and then relieved. His sister said this was the correct order for his feelings. He had not lost earned public pay, but he would still lose the opportunity of a private loaded job his wrist could not accept. Yue carried his actual restriction into the closing schedule only with his agreement. Recovery stayed slower than the town's appetite for completion.

canal_p21_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_068.text: The appointed assistant checked the next cause-hearing notice against its actual date: the fifty-second day. The earlier quarry drainage inspection had found a raised private stock bank narrowing the required free outlet width. Broader responsibility for individual losses remained for the hearing, with current evidence and replies needed. Yue sorted the rainfall reports, downstream observations, and paid repair records so dates could be compared. A storm had not waited for their documents, but the documents could still prevent one dramatic moment from swallowing every other fact about the loss.

canal_p21_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_069.text: The quarry owner sent his chosen representative with the permit copy and the outlet correction bill. The public drainage officer would present the observed narrowing and the later accepted correction from his own inspection. Neither Yue nor Luo had secretly inspected inaccessible ground upriver. Their commission's evidence came from dated messages, current lower measurements, and the actual route observations they had made. Yue prepared to answer questions about those limits. Tian told her she sounded as if she expected cross-examination by a wet boulder. Yue replied that boulders at least rarely changed their story after reading a bill.

canal_p21_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_070.text: The gardener brought her seed purchase receipt for the claims file, with the private support and household food grain kept separate. The reed household chose to submit the actual roof replacement price and remaining lost stock account. The stall owner would bring her spoiled ingredients' paid quantities and the extra private market sales that reduced her loss. All three retained their claims despite the earlier ten-copper hardship support. No waiver had been hidden in the money or twelve food sacks. Yue arranged their chosen pages beside the source notes and resisted compressing them into a single neat tragedy.

canal_p21_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_071.text: The new assistant found a duplicated roof total copied once as a bill and once as a household account of paying it. She flagged the matching date and receiver before the hearing packet went out. Pei checked it and retained the household's words without adding the same expense twice. The reed cutter laughed when told. "I would happily suffer the roof twice if someone bought it twice." His wife elbowed him and approved the corrected amount. Yue enjoyed the joke because the correction had occurred before anyone needed to defend a larger number as a matter of pride.

canal_p21_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_072.text: Luo checked the winter keys and receiver contacts before coming to the hearing. Her standing work continued; she could not spend the whole next day arguing over losses while the canal looked after itself. The young keeper accepted the ordinary morning round within their current schedule. No emergency operator was quietly called back. The disconnected frame and eight charged stones stayed dry in their recorded custody. Yue checked the case seal with the keeper and then went home to eat. There would be enough questions tomorrow without creating a new failure through hungry, exhausted preparation.

canal_p21_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_073.text: Ren's appointment remained the fifty-ninth morning, with the full accepted review interval. The booked ordinary departure followed canal closure on the fifty-seventh day. Yue had paid the three-copper fare and held four copper for beds and food; the optional kiln copper would only be used if her final itinerary took that connection. She told the passage agent no new public task had extended her term. He kept the reserved place. A rumor about the forgotten return would not become a reason to miss a second accepted date. The future road office had the separate repair request it actually needed.

canal_p21_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_074.text: The personal orchard papers remained separate from the cause-hearing folder. Yue noticed that she was reaching for them whenever the public preparation felt uncertain. She put them away deliberately and finished labeling the lower observations. Returning to one obligation did not excuse neglecting the closing work of another. This time she needed no grand promise to herself. The next real task was a date on a wet-weather note that Pei could no longer read comfortably. Yue read it aloud, checked the source, and made a broad copy. Then she left the office before the lamp burned low.

canal_p21_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_075.text: At the quiet supper bend Luo ate from her own bowl while standing on the sound permitted yard edge. She could no longer use the damaged return as an easy hiding place, and the cabinet maker was nearby planing a rack. They spoke about the weather without arguing about title. Yue came only to return the broad warning copy. The keeper asked her to wait while she finished eating, not to inspect anything else. For a few minutes the canal was simply water beside two people's supper. Yue had almost forgotten it could serve that purpose too.

canal_p21_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_076.text: Han and his wife practiced the cause-hearing account after closing the private store. They would acknowledge the old sale notice's unsupported claims, the returned forty-eight deposit, and the valid remaining fifty-six loan without letting that account decide quarry losses. Han wanted to explain his mother's flood memory. His wife said there would be time if the question called for it. Yue heard only part of the conversation while passing and kept walking. Private rehearsal was not public evidence offered for her approval. She could meet his actual statement tomorrow without collecting every unfinished word on the way.

canal_p21_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_077.text: Tian stayed up late checking the real sail's last seam, then stopped before tired fingers began to make new errors. The fitting on the fifty-fifth afternoon had its customer and observer confirmed. Her mother had agreed to attend and bring food rather than an argument prepared in advance. Yue wished her good night from the doorway. The plant's new leaf held firm in the stove-room window. If Tian chose the winter trial after passing, Luo would tend it under their actual little arrangement. The possible departure no longer looked like abandoning everything rooted in town.

canal_p21_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p21_078.text: The fifty-first night closed with the old return shown, its damage marked, private goods removed, and a separate estimate request acknowledged. The town had not become richer by discovering a line on a map. It had become harder to sell that line as private convenience or forget it until a child fell through the edge. Yue rested her writing hand and listened to an ordinary boat pass the safe landing. Tomorrow the cause hearing would put loss and responsibility into the same room. She would arrive with what she had actually seen, and let other people answer for the rest.
